the CGC picture of small-x nuclear wavefunctions is able to successfully predict the observed suppression of forward particle production in d+Au, and that the CGC framework can be used to make predictions for the azimuthal correlation of forward dijets.

(i) The CGC picture of the small-x wavefunction successfully predicts the suppression of high-pT particle production at forward rapidities, (ii) the CGC predicts that the azimuthal correlation of forward dijets is strongly modified in d+Au relative to p+p.

the azimuthal angle correlations between forward dijets in high-energy d+Au collisions are sensitive to the nonlinear QCD evolution of the small-x gluons, and that they can be used to test the CGC picture of the initial state at RHIC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CGC picture of the nuclear structure function is consistent with the data, but the CGC description of jet production is not.
the CGC picture of the initial nuclear state is consistent with the experimental data at forward rapidity.
the forward dijet correlations are a powerful probe of the CGC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
forward dijets are strongly correlated in d+Au, with a correlation function that is significantly different from the one of p+p collisions.
the azimuthal correlation between two high-pT particles produced at forward rapidity in d+Au is dominated by the nonlinear QCD evolution of the nuclear wave function at small-x.
the azimuthal angle between dijets at forward and backward rapidities can be used to probe the small-x nuclear gluon distribution, and to test whether it is universal or not.
